chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Lead sheets, repertoire and the burden of 'Loch Lomond'
summary: She writes lead sheets for her accompanists, fields 'why did you sing Loch Lomond', and says the song has gotten her out of bad situations.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: So I'd make out a lead sheet with the chords on there and give it to the piano player and we'd try it and if it worked out well we'd put it back

into the repertoire again. So, and of course they're new to alot of people. In fact, I did "Loch Loman" the other night and you won't believe this, I tried not to do it. I tried not to push it down anybody's throat. So just last Saturday I was working out in Atlantic Beach in a room that Mosey Alexander, the drummer has something to do with. Of course Mosey has had a stroke. He's not there now. His son is playing drums. But there was a woman there and she insisted upon my doing "Loch Loman". Well I put her off until the last minute and I did it. And when I got through singing there was a party there and I went over to talk to them. They wanted to know why did I do "Loch Loman". They had never heard of Maxine Sullivan or "Loch Loman".

Why did you sing "Loch Loman"? Wow, so I had to go through the whole bit about in 1937 how I recorded it and it put me on the map. So I guess it has got to be a novelty coming to a night club after singing "Saint Louis Blues" and you do "Loch Loman". But I do "Loch Loman" and do "Saint Louis Blues" afterwards. But you never know. It's a strange thing, you know.

You never thought of kind of putting you foot down and saying, I will never sing that song again and make a resolution?

Not really because "Loch Lomond" has sort of gotten me out of a bad situation on alot of occasions because you know, if you sing standard pop tunes okay, but if there is anybody there who know that you do "Loch Lomond" - in fact, invirably, If I appear someplace the publicity always says, "The 'Loch Lomond' Girl". So they expect to hear "Loch Lomond". And I suppose if they didn't have the "Loch Lomond Girl" then I wouldn't be the attraction. You got to have some reason to be there. There are singers and performers who never get a song that they can be identified with, or do anything that they're identified with. / So I can't knock it. I don't enjoy having to do it every night but that's the theme song. We don't use it in the early days, you know, when I was traveling alot. I used to use "Loch Lomond", say sixteen bars of "Loch Lomond" as entrance music, you know, to identify my theme song. But we don't do that anymore. We just go right on and whatever my first song is that's what we do.
Sophie Tucker's "Some Of These Days" is her theme song.
